first.rationale: We face simultaneous activation and onboarding headwinds (both down ~4-6% QoQ) alongside competitive price pressure. Verifying memory_86 and memory_91 confirms the durability of onboarding simplification and activation messaging gains before committing. Activation messaging showed direct week-one engagement lift (memory_91) and works complementarily with shortened onboarding (memory_86). This combination addresses the immediate activation decline without committing long-term margin erosion through promotional pricing. While promotional pricing (memory_73) tempts given competitive pressure, it risks a race to the bottom on unit economics and treats a symptom rather than the core engagement problem. Referral incentives (memory_57) work best on *established* cohorts during healthy periods, not during acquisition headwinds. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the SMB activation crisis. A standard_experiment on activation_messaging, informed by verification of the two most relevant prior wins, balances speed, evidence, and sustainable revenue quality. We preserve uncertainty by running standard scope, not broad rollout, and allow pivots if verification surfaces data degradation in the archived records.

final.rationale: Verification confirms both memory_86 (onboarding completion +13%, retention +3%) and memory_91 (week-one engagement +11%, activation +6%, retention +1%) as durable wins. We are running activation_messaging at standard_experiment scale this week. The archival data shows in-product messaging directly lifted activation by 6 percentage points with measurable retention durability—precisely what we need to counter the current 6% QoQ activation decline. We are not running onboarding simplification again (already deployed in memory_31 baseline) but instead layering activation_messaging on top. This addresses the immediate engagement crisis without margin erosion or ecosystem harm. Promotional pricing remains a fallback for future weeks if competitive pressure intensifies and messaging alone does not arrest the decline. Standard experiment scope allows rapid learnings before any broad rollout, preserving our ability to adjust if new data emerges.
